proposal:
# Re-rank proposal 2026-10-30 (8): loop boundary after card 209

- Led by: the product manager seat (fresh context, pm-rerank-8; Claude because the 16:24 UTC probes (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota). Proposal for objection window (D153); the facilitator opens it and polls.
- Before (note 7): 209, 210, 208, 211, 217, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207; unranked: 218, 219.
- After: 210, 219, 208, 211, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207 (209 out: work, review, gate and sign-off are on origin; only its held record and the issue close wait on 219).
  - 210 (corrective for MD-003): first; startable now. Small, and it makes the records that 208 writes trustworthy.
  - 219 (record checker accepts out-of-order closes, D159): second; needs a Decider to start (see Gate below). It must land before 208 closes, because 208 closing after 210 hits the same refusal as 209 (210's evidence would predate 208's record), and it releases 209's held record and 213's close.
  - 208 (corrective for MD-002): third; startable now. Large (the architect splits it), so 219 can land while it runs.
  - 211 (corrective for MD-010): fourth; startable now. Records only, no code, independent of the rest.
  - 217 (thread-pool starvation, bug): fifth, not second. It is not corrective for any open FAIL, and its scope needs a text refresh first (see below). Ahead of every non-corrective card.
  - 218 (mid-card retro removal keeps the seat): sixth. Hardens the just-shipped 209 rule; depends on 209, whose code is on origin. Behind the cards that unblock closes or reduce red CI.
  - 213 (checker rejects an incomplete objection window): seventh. Unchanged work, needs 219 to close; gate-blocked until the FAILs clear.
  - 216, 212, 215, 206, 207: unchanged relative order; none names an open FAIL, so none can start while MD-002, MD-003, MD-010 are open.
- Next card: 210 (the first card in order that the gate lets start).
- Rationale (one line): only 210, 208 and 211 are startable, 219 is the one non-corrective card that must land before the second corrective card can close, and 217 follows them because a flaky red does not tax the mob-defaults gate runs and its scope is stale.

## What changed and why

- 209 leaves the list; 219 enters second and 218 sixth, both new.
- Gate (the facilitator starts only cards whose issue names an open FAIL). Open FAILs per audit 42 (.mob/audits/last.json): MD-002, MD-003, MD-010.
  - Startable with no change: 210 (names MD-003), 208 (names MD-002), 211 (names MD-010).
  - Not startable: 219 (names no finding; its issue says it is not corrective), 218 (names only MD-001, which audit 42 lists closed), 217 (names F-063, now a FLAG, and F-065, closed), and 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207.
  - Needs a Decider: 219, as a one-card exemption (a defect in the checker that blocks 209's record and would block 208's close). It is not a gate change for other cards. Do not edit the issue text of 219, 218 or 217 to name MD-002, MD-003 or MD-010: they do not fix them. If the live register still holds MD-001 open (the brief says 209's record must land first; audit 42 says closed on git evidence), 219 and 218 can instead truthfully add "Corrective action for MD-001" by a card-text window, and no Decider is needed; the facilitator should read the register before choosing.
  - Fallback with no Decider: run 208 before 210 (number order) so no close is refused; this costs "210 enables 208" and is worse than the Decider.
- 217 stays behind the corrective cards, against the product owner / auditor proposal to rank it second. Reasons: (1) it cannot start while the FAILs are open whatever its rank, so rank 2 would not start it, only block the order; (2) 210, 208 and 211 are mob-defaults cards gated by that repository's Python tests, and the phrase-lang pre-push hook runs only mob_process.py check, so the acceptance-suite flake taxes phrase-lang CI pushes, not these three gates; (3) F-063 is a FLAG at audit 40, the 128 thread-pool floor from 214 commit 5b is still in place, and CI was green on 214's shipping commit. The flaky-tests-are-bugs rule is kept: 217 is the first non-corrective card and starts the moment the gate allows it. If the team wants it earlier, that is a second Decider exemption, and I do not propose it.
- 217 scope (card-text fix for its task-force window at ready, D153): its text calls F-063 and F-065 open FAILs and owns three "environmental" tests. The auditor reads those as staleness, not flakes: Bar6 is the suspended Usable-v1 bar 6 that card 162 restores; the two CSharpBaseline tests report tests_did_not_run. Thread-pool work will not fix them, and Done check 3 (two identical full runs) cannot pass while they fail. Proposed: 217 keeps F-063 and the blocking ReadToEnd and WaitForExit scan; the three tests are root-caused and either given their own bug cards (Bar6 under card 162) or recorded as excluded from Done check 3 with the cause named; the source line is updated to FLAG and closed.
- 218 and 219 move from unranked to ranked; both depend on cards already on origin.

## Evidence considered

- Blocker .mob/records/blockers/2026-10-30-209-record-order.md; D159 (docs/decisions/process-and-staffing.md); issues 217, 218, 219 read live (updated 15:58, 12:54, 16:36 UTC) and the board copies of 208, 210, 211, 213.
- The checker rule in the blocker: a card's evidence is compared with the record of the next-lower card number, so 210 closing before 208 is refused when 208's record is added.
- corrective_gate_message in mob-defaults mob_process.py (exact-token match against blocking findings only).
- .mob/audits/last.json (audit 42, 16:32 UTC): open FAILs MD-002, MD-003, MD-010; MD-001 closed on git evidence. This is newer than the audit 40 facts in the brief.
- Not seen: .mob/findings.json is not in this repository (card 206 adds the mirror), so the live register could not be read here.
- .githooks/pre-push and .github/workflows/ci.yml (hook runs the process check only; CI runs the full dotnet suite).
- Notes 6, 6b and 7 for the 217 history and the earlier "take it to a Decider rather than bypass the gate" position.

## Neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change

Reversible: it only reorders a list and adds two cards; any card can be moved again at the next boundary. It applies the corrective-card gate as written (nothing is exempted by this note; the one Decider request for 219 is a separate decision) and the flaky-tests-are-bugs rule as written. No checker, template or gate text changes.

## Window rule

Every declared role polled (F-054): the roles declared for the window by the facilitator (architect, QA engineer, backend developer, independent reviewer (audit lens), delivery lead, product manager (signoff) in windows 6b and 7); the product manager is the proposer; silence is not consent.
